data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Israeli soldier accused of smearing faeces on Palestinian detainee’s face
An Israeli soldier has been accused of abusing a Palestinian detainee at a military outpost in the occupied West Bank, including beating him, urinating on him and smearing faeces on his face.
According to Israel’s Channel 12 News, the abuse took place last month at the Jalameh military outpost, after Israeli soldiers arrested a Palestinian man at a nearby crossing.
The soldiers reportedly found a small knife in his car. The Palestinian was later released without charge.
The soldiers initially transferred him to the outpost handcuffed and blindfolded, where military police investigators suspect one of them began abusing him.

Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen has declined to rule out the suggestion that discussions are taking place over sweeping restrictions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), following a report that the Netherlands is negotiating with Washington over changes that could severely undermine the court's powers.
Questioned in parliament on Wednesday, Berendsen said diplomatic discussions were taking place but he would not specify whether proposals to shield heads of state and restrict the court's jurisdiction over nationals of non-member states were under consideration.
The exchange followed a report by Dutch rights organisation The Rights Forum, citing anonymous diplomatic sources in New York, that the Netherlands was "negotiating" with the US changes to the court's founding treaty in response to US sanctions on the court and its top officials.
Middle East Eye has previously reported similar US demands.
In December 2025, MEE exclusively revealed that Washington had pressed for an end to the Palestine and Afghanistan investigations and treaty changes preventing prosecutions of nationals of non-member countries, in return for lifting sanctions.
Athough the US is not a member state of the ICC, its sanctions and recent threats to "dismantle" the court are prompted mainly by Washington's opposition to the prosecution of Israeli leaders and the court's ability to also prosecute US officials for crimes committed on the territory of member states.

X suspends campaign account of Palestinian American running for US Senate
A Palestinian American who launched his bid for a Senate seat to represent Pennsylvania in the 2028 election has had his campaign account suspended by the social media platform X.
The account, @moorforpa, belongs to Gaza-born, Philadelphia-raised Ahmed Moor, who said this week he wants to topple hardline pro-Israel Senator John Fetterman when he's up for re-election in two years.
Fetterman has not announced whether he plans to run again.
"FRIENDS! It's official! We're a threat," Moor wrote on his personal X account on Wednesday. "They've suspended the campaign account. Help us maintain the momentum by retweeting and please consider donating."

US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries wants 'dramatic change' in Middle East
US House of Representatives Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries called on Thursday for "dramatic change" in the Middle East and reiterated his support for a two-state solution for Israelis and the Palestinians.
The Democrats' sweeping victories in last week's midterm elections could lead to the curbing of US support for its close ally Israel, putting the spotlight on party leaders' views as they prepare to take control of both houses of Congress on 3 January.
Jeffries, a New York Democrat, is expected to be the next House speaker.
"The status quo is unacceptable, and we need dramatic change. And that looks like, as far as I'm concerned, making sure you have a safe and secure Israel, living side by side as a Jewish and democratic state with an independent Palestinian state that provides dignity and self-determination for the Palestinians," he said at a weekly press conference.

data.author: Bilge Kotan

Trump sidelines Vance from Iran talks, says no need to negotiate
President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the US is no longer interested in negotiations with Iran, as he appeared to sideline his own vice president, JD Vance, who has tried to position himself as a mediator in the war.
“We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed…We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Trump wrote on social media, referring to the Hormuz waterway.
Trump’s statement is a flip-flop of his comments earlier this week saying that there was “momentum” for a political settlement with Iran and that negotiations were ongoing.
He appeared to relegate Vance to handling a new domestic file of what he called the “corrupt disasters” of Democrat-run cities and states.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli settlers injure five Palestinians
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Israeli settlers injure five Palestinians
Israeli settlers stormed Atara, a Palestinian village in the occupied West Bank and injured five people on Thursday, a rights group said.
The attacks came after the Israeli military took down two outposts built by settlers without permission in the West Bank.
More than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements across the West Bank, all of which are deemed illegal under international law, and some of which, known as outposts, are built without the Israeli government's involvement.
"After Israeli military forces left the area, dozens of settlers, armed with clubs, tear gas and stones, stormed the village of Atara," the Israeli rights group Yesh Din said in a statement.
"Five residents were injured and hospitalised, one in serious condition with a brain haemorrhage," Yesh Din added.
The Palestinian Red Crescent said one of the injured people was 67 years old.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Pro-Palestinian group seeks ban on Israeli real estate fair in Paris
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Pro-Palestinian group seeks ban on Israeli real estate fair in Paris
Pro-Palestinian activists have asked a French court to ban an Israeli real estate fair in Paris marketing Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem, AFP reported on Thursday.
The Franco-Palestinian NIDAL association filed an emergency motion with a court against the 9th Icube real estate and investment salon, arguing that the fair violates human rights.
The event is scheduled for Sunday at the European Centre for Judaism in the French capital. Other major cities have seen similar uproars over Israeli real estate fairs.
NIDAL asked the court to either order the head of the Paris police force to ban the event outright or to ensure that the event does not sell property in the West Bank and East Jerusalem, whose occupation by Israel since 1967 is considered illegal under international law.
Before taking legal action, the group said they had sent a letter to the Paris police on 5 November, which went unanswered.
In the filing, seen by AFP, the rights group says that marketing Israeli settlements in the occupied territories contributes to the forced displacement of the Palestinian people through population transfer - a practice prohibited by international law and classified as a war crime under the French penal code.
In particular, the activists highlighted that BH Nadlan, a company that markets settlements in both East Jerusalem and the West Bank on its website, will be present at the fair.
They also pointed to the fair's official guide's offer of a "significant" financial "bonus" for newcomers settling in "Judea and Samaria", the Israeli term for the occupied West Bank.

data.author: Bilge Kotan

Bethlehem Church of the Nativity priest denied visa to speak at US event
Father Issa Thaljieh, the Palestinian parish priest at the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem, in the occupied West Bank, has been denied a US visa to speak alongside American clergy next week on the gravity of Israeli settler attacks on Palestinian villages.
"Our government denied him a visa for 'security reasons'. A parish priest from Bethlehem, treated as a threat. That should worry all of us, because it means the people living through this are being kept from telling us about it," Laila Mokhiber, a volunteer with Orthodox Christians for Palestine (OCP), told Middle East Eye on Thursday.
MEE has reached out to the State Department.
Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant leaders are set to gather at the United Methodist Building near the US Capitol on Monday to demand that Congress hold accountable both settlers and the Israeli military, and also curb US weapons transfers to Israel.

data.title: Middle East Eye: How Western media framed the Israeli attack on Nasser Hospital
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
How Western media framed the Israeli attack on Nasser Hospital
On MEE Live, presenter James Schneider examines how Western media coverage obscured Israel's attack on Gaza’s Nasser Hospital on Thursday.
At least seven Palestinians, including a doctor and patients, were killed in an Israeli air strike on the hospital in Khan Younis. Over dozens of others were wounded, with the strike damaging the hospital's surgical wing.
Schneider highlights the framing used by The New York Times, which had Israeli claims that Hamas had established a command centre inside the hospital complex in the subheading.
The attack comes amid continued Israeli violations of the October 2025 ceasefire and a wider assault on Gaza's healthcare infrastructure. More than 1,800 medical facilities have been partially or completely destroyed since the genocide began, according to a joint UN, World Bank and EU assessment.
